此示例展示了实现 debugFillProperties 的最佳实践，说明如何使用所有常见的 DiagnosticsProperty 子类，以及此类属性的常用 DiagnosticsProperty 参数。
link 
class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

widgets/Element/dependOnInheritedWidgetO.0: 返回给定类型 T 的最近 widget，并建立对它的依赖；如果未找到合适的 widget，则返回 null。
widgets/Element/dependOnInheritedWidgetO.1: 找到的 widget 将是具体的 InheritedWidget 子类。调用 dependOnInheritedWidgetOfExactType 会将此构建上下文注册到返回的 widget 上。当该 widget 发生变化（或出现同类型的新 widget，或该 widget 被移除）时，此构建上下文会重新构建，以便从该 widget 获取新值。
widgets/Element/dependOnInheritedWidgetO.2: 通常会通过 of() 静态方法隐式调用此方法，例如 Theme.of。
widgets/Element/dependOnInheritedWidgetO.3: 不应在 widget 构造函数或 State.initState 方法中调用此方法。虽然调用此方法实际上会将 BuildContext 注册为依赖项，以便将来重新构建，但构造函数和 State.initState 受生命周期限制，只会在 element 初次创建时执行一次。
widgets/Element/dependOnInheritedWidgetO.4: 如果继承值之后发生变化，框架会正确触发 State.build 再次运行，但无法重新运行构造函数或 State.initState。因此，如果这些只执行一次的方法使用继承值的“快照”初始化了内部变量、控制器或副作用，它们就会保留最初的、如今已过时的值。这会导致状态不同步：widget 的 State.build 可能使用了更新后的数据，而内部逻辑仍依赖在 State.initState 期间捕获的旧数据。
widgets/Element/dependOnInheritedWidgetO.5: 为确保 widget 保持同步，应从 build 方法、布局和绘制回调，或 State.didChangeDependencies 中直接或间接调用此方法。
widgets/Element/dependOnInheritedWidgetO.6: State.didChangeDependencies 会紧接着 State.initState 调用；每当此上下文所依赖的继承 widget 发生变化时，都会再次调用，直到 widget 或其某个祖先下次移动为止（例如添加或移除祖先）。这样，State 就可以在调用 State.build 之前，更新内部变量或执行依赖继承值的初始化逻辑。
widgets/Element/dependOnInheritedWidgetO.7: 由于此时 element 树不再稳定，不应从 State.dispose 中调用此方法。若要在该方法中引用祖先，应在 State.didChangeDependencies 中保存对祖先的引用。可以在 State.deactivate 中安全地使用此方法；widget 从树中移除时会调用该方法。
widgets/Element/dependOnInheritedWidgetO.8: 也可以在交互事件处理器（例如手势回调）或计时器中调用此方法，以便获取一次值，前提是不缓存该值，也不在之后重复使用。
widgets/Element/dependOnInheritedWidgetO.9: 此方法的时间复杂度为 O(1)，且常数因子较小，但会导致 widget 更频繁地重新构建。
widgets/Element/dependOnInheritedWidgetO.10: 只有当 T 是支持局部更新的 InheritedWidget 子类（例如 InheritedModel）时，才会使用 aspect 参数。该参数指定此上下文所依赖的继承 widget 的哪个“方面”。

widgets/Element/inflateWidget.html.1: 此方法通常由 updateChild 调用，但需要更精细地控制 element 创建过程的子类也可以直接调用。
widgets/Element/inflateWidget.html.2: 如果给定 widget 带有全局 key，且已有 element 的 widget 使用了相同的全局 key，此函数会复用该 element（可能将其从树中的其他位置移接过来，或从非活动 element 列表中重新激活），而不是创建新的 element。
widgets/Element/inflateWidget.html.3: newSlot 参数指定此 element 的 slot 新值。
widgets/Element/inflateWidget.html.4: 此函数返回的 element 已经挂载，并处于“活动”生命周期状态。

widgets/Element/markNeedsBuild.html.0: 将此 element 标记为脏状态，并将其加入全局 widget 列表，以便在下一帧重新构建。

widgets/Element/mount.html.0: 将此 element 添加到给定父级的指定插槽中。

widgets/Element/mount.html.2: 此方法会将 element 从“初始”生命周期状态转换为“活动”状态。
widgets/Element/mount.html.3: 重写此方法的子类通常也需要重写 update、visitChildren、RenderObjectElement.insertRenderObjectChild、RenderObjectElement.moveRenderObjectChild 和 RenderObjectElement.removeRenderObjectChild。
widgets/Element/mount.html.4: 此方法的实现应先调用继承的方法，例如 super.mount(parent, newSlot)。

widgets/Element/mounted.html.0: 与此上下文关联的 Widget 当前是否已挂载到 widget 树中。
widgets/Element/mounted.html.1: 只有当 mounted 为 true 时，才能访问 BuildContext 的属性或调用其方法。如果 mounted 为 false，断言就会触发。
widgets/Element/mounted.html.2: 给定的 BuildContext 一旦卸载，就永远不会再次挂载。
widgets/Element/mounted.html.3: 如果在异步间隙中使用 BuildContext（即执行异步操作后继续使用），请考虑先检查 mounted，以确定上下文仍然有效，再与其交互：

widgets/Element/operator_equals.html.0: 比较两个 widget 是否相等。
widgets/Element/operator_equals.html.1: 如果某个 widget 重新构建后与另一个 widget 根据 operator == 比较相等，框架就会认为此次更新是多余的，并跳过对树中该分支的更新工作。

widgets/Element/operator_equals.html.3: 对于叶子 widget（没有子项的 widget），有时重写此方法是合理的：前提是已知重新构建该 widget 的成本远高于检查其参数是否相等，并且预计该 widget 经常以相同参数重新构建。
widgets/Element/operator_equals.html.4: 不过通常来说，如果已知 build 方法中使用的 widget 不会变化，缓存这些 widget 会更高效。

widgets/Element/owner.html.0: 管理此元素生命周期的对象。

widgets/Element/performRebuild.html.1: 完成相应检查后，由 rebuild 调用。
widgets/Element/performRebuild.html.2: 基类实现只会清除 dirty 标志。

widgets/Element/reassemble.html.0: 调试期间每当应用重新组装时调用，例如执行热重载时。
widgets/Element/reassemble.html.1: 此方法应重新运行所有依赖全局状态的初始化逻辑，例如从资源包加载图像（因为资源包可能已更改）。
widgets/Element/reassemble.html.2: 此函数只会在开发期间调用。发布版本中没有 ext.flutter.reassemble 钩子，因此这段代码永远不会执行。
widgets/Element/reassemble.html.3: 实现者不应依赖热重载启动后，热重载源码更新、reassemble 和 build 方法之间的调用顺序。可能会有 Timer（例如 Animation）或附加到 isolate 的调试会话，在调用 reassemble 之前就使用重新加载的代码触发 build。依赖热重载后由 reassemble 设置前置条件的代码，必须能够应对调用顺序错乱，例如在条件不满足时安全退出，而不是抛出异常。尽管如此，reassemble 一旦调用，之后至少会调用一次 build。

widgets/Element/rebuild.html.0: 使 widget 更新自身。在调试构建中，还会验证各种不变量。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.1: 当 BuildOwner.scheduleBuildFor 被调用以将此 element 标记为脏状态时，BuildOwner 会调用此方法；element 首次构建时，mount 会调用此方法；widget 发生变化时，update 也会调用此方法。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.2: 只有当 dirty 为 true 时，此方法才会重新构建。若要忽略 dirty 标志并强制重新构建，请将 force 设为 true。在 update 中强制重新构建很方便，因为此时 dirty 为 false。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.5: Widget 表示 Element 的配置。每个 Element 都有一个 widget，由 Element.widget 指定。日常表述中常会使用“widget”，即使严格来说“element”才更准确。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.6: Element 会持有当前的 Widget，但随着时间推移，该 widget 可能被其他 widget 替换。例如，支撑 ColoredBox 的 element 最初可能持有一个 ColoredBox，其 ColoredBox.color 为蓝色，之后又被赋予一个颜色为绿色的新 ColoredBox。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.7: 在同一时刻，同一棵树中的多个 Element 可以持有相同的 Widget。例如，同一个绿色的 ColoredBox 可以同时用于 widget 树中的多个位置，每个位置都由不同的 Element 支撑。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.8: 将 element 标记为脏状态
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.9: Element 可以在帧与帧之间被标记为脏状态。可能的原因包括：
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.10: StatefulWidget 的 State 可以通过调用 State.setState 方法，将其 Element 标记为脏状态。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.11: InheritedWidget 发生变化时，先前订阅了它的后代会被标记为脏状态。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.12: 热重载期间，每个 element 都会被标记为脏状态（通过 Element.reassemble）。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.14: 脏 element 会在下一帧重新构建。具体方式取决于 element 的类型。StatelessElement 使用其 widget 的 StatelessWidget.build 方法重新构建。StatefulElement 使用其 widget 的 state 的 State.build 方法重新构建。RenderObjectElement 则通过更新其 RenderObject 来重新构建。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.15: 在许多情况下，重新构建的最终结果是一个子 widget，或者（对于 MultiChildRenderObjectElement）是一组子 widget。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.16: 这些子 widget 用于更新 element 的子 element（或多个子 element）的 widget 属性。如果新 Widget 与现有 Element 具有相同的 Type 和 Key，就认为它们相对应。（对于 MultiChildRenderObjectElement，框架还会尽力跟踪顺序发生变化的 widget；详见 RenderObjectElement.updateChildren。）
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.17: 如果没有对应的旧子项，就会创建一个新的 Element（使用 Widget.createElement）；随后该 element 本身也会递归地构建。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.18: 如果之前存在子项，但本次构建没有提供与之对应的子项来更新它，则会丢弃旧子项（若涉及 GlobalKey 重新挂载，也可能在 element 树的其他位置重用该子项）。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.19: 不过，最常见的情况是存在对应的旧子项。此时会让该子 Element 使用新的子 Widget 更新自身。对于 StatefulElement，这会触发 State.didUpdateWidget。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.21: 在告知 Element 使用新的 Widget 更新自身之前，会先使用 operator == 比较新旧对象。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.22: 通常，这相当于使用 identical 进行比较，以确认两个对象是否确实是同一个实例。如果是同一实例，且该 element 没有因其他原因被标记为脏状态，那么它就会跳过更新，因为可以确定更新自身及其后代没有任何益处。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.23: 强烈建议不要为 Widget 对象重写 operator ==。虽然这样看似可以提升性能，但对于非叶子 widget，实际上会导致 O(N²) 的行为。这是因为比较必然需要比较子 widget；如果这些子 widget 也实现了 operator ==，最终就会遍历整个 widget 树……而且树的每一层都会重复遍历。实际上，直接重新构建更省开销。（此外，只要应用中使用的 Widget 子类有任何一个实现了 operator ==，编译器就无法在任何位置内联该比较，因为它必须将调用视为虚调用，以防实例恰好属于重写了该运算符的类型。）
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.24: 避免不必要重新构建的最佳方式，是缓存从 State.build 返回的 widget，使每一帧都使用相同的 widget，直到它们发生变化。有几种机制可以帮助做到这一点，例如 const widget 就是一种自动缓存形式（如果使用 const 关键字构造 widget，那么每次以相同参数构造时都会返回同一个实例）。
widgets/Element/rebuild.html.25: 另一个例子是 AnimatedBuilder.child 属性：即使 AnimatedBuilder.builder 回调重新创建其他组件，它也能让子树中不参与动画的部分保持不变。

widgets/Element/renderObject.html.0: 树中此位置（或其下方位置）上的渲染对象。
widgets/Element/renderObject.html.1: 如果此对象是 RenderObjectElement，则渲染对象就是树中此位置上的对象。否则，此 getter 会沿树向下遍历，直到找到 RenderObjectElement。

widgets/Element/slot.html.0: 由父级设置的信息，用于定义此子项在父级子项列表中的位置。

widgets/Element/toDiagnosticsNode.html.0: 返回此对象的调试表示形式，供调试工具和 DiagnosticsNode.toStringDeep 使用。

widgets/Element/unmount.html.0: 从“非活动”生命周期状态转换为“失效”状态。

widgets/Element/unmount.html.4: 有关详细信息，请参阅 Element 的生命周期文档。
widgets/Element/unmount.html.5: 此方法的实现应以调用继承的方法结束，例如 super.unmount()。

widgets/Element/update.html.0: 更改用于配置此 element 的 widget。
widgets/Element/update.html.1: 父级希望使用不同的 widget 配置此 element 时，框架会调用此函数。新 widget 的 runtimeType 保证与旧 widget 相同。
widgets/Element/update.html.2: 此函数只会在“活动”生命周期状态下调用。

widgets/Element/updateChild.html.0: 使用给定的新配置更新给定的子项。
widgets/Element/updateChild.html.1: 此方法是 widget 系统的核心。每当需要根据更新后的配置添加、更新或移除子项时，都会调用它。
widgets/Element/updateChild.html.2: newSlot 参数指定此 element 的 slot 新值。
widgets/Element/updateChild.html.3: 如果 child 为 null，而 newWidget 不为 null，则表示有一个新子项，需要为其创建一个使用 newWidget 配置的 Element。
widgets/Element/updateChild.html.4: 如果 newWidget 为 null，而 child 不为 null，则需要移除该子项，因为它已不再有配置。
widgets/Element/updateChild.html.5: 如果两者都不为 null，则需要将 child 的配置更新为 newWidget 给出的新配置。如果现有子项可以接受 newWidget（由 Widget.canUpdate 判断），就会将其交给该子项；否则，需要释放旧子项，并为新配置创建一个子项。

widgets/Element/updateChild.html.7: updateChild 方法会返回新创建的子项（如果需要创建），或传入并更新后的子项，或在移除子项且未替换时返回 null。
widgets/Element/updateChild.html.9: 仅当 newWidget 不为 null 时才会使用 newSlot 参数。如果 child 为 null（或旧子项无法更新），则会通过 inflateWidget 将 newSlot 传给为该子项创建的新 Element。如果 child 不为 null（且旧子项可以更新），则会将 newSlot 传给 updateSlotForChild 来更新其 slot，以应对它自上次构建以来发生的位置变化。
widgets/Element/updateChild.html.10: 有关 slot 的更多信息，请参阅 RenderObjectElement 文档。

widgets/Element/updateChildren.html.0: 更新此 element 的子项，使其使用新的 widget。
widgets/Element/updateChildren.html.1: 尝试使用给定的新 widget 更新给定的旧子项列表，按需移除过时的 element 并添加新的 element，然后返回新的子项列表。
widgets/Element/updateChildren.html.2: 执行此函数期间，不得修改 oldChildren 列表。如果调用方希望在此函数仍在调用栈中时重入并移除 oldChildren 中的 element，可以提供 forgottenChildren 参数，并在此函数执行期间修改它。每当此函数读取 oldChildren 时，都会先检查该子项是否位于 forgottenChildren 中。如果在其中，此函数就会将其视为不在 oldChildren 中。

widgets/Element/updateChildren.html.4: 当 slot 值变化时，其 Element 关联的 renderObject 需要移动到其父级子项列表中的新位置。如果该 RenderObject 使用链表组织子项（如 ContainerRenderObjectMixin 所做），则可将子项 RenderObject 重新插入到与 IndexedSlot.value 所指定 Element 关联的 RenderObject 之后；该值来自 slot 对象。

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

This example shows best practices for implementing debugFillProperties illustrating use of all common DiagnosticsProperty subclasses and all common DiagnosticsProperty parameters.
link 
class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

This example shows best practices for implementing debugFillProperties illustrating use of all common DiagnosticsProperty subclasses and all common DiagnosticsProperty parameters.
link 
class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

widgets/Flex/direction.html.1: 如果轴向已知，可考虑改用 Row（水平）或 Column（垂直），而不是 Flex，因为写法更简洁。（对 Row 和 Column 来说，此属性固定为相应的轴向。）

widgets/Flex/Flex.html.2: 如果 crossAxisAlignment 为 CrossAxisAlignment.baseline，则 textBaseline 不能为 null。
widgets/Flex/Flex.html.3: textDirection 参数默认采用环境中的 Directionality（如果存在）。如果不存在环境方向信息，且需要根据文本方向决定子项的布局方向，或需要明确主轴或交叉轴方向上的 start／end 含义，则 textDirection 不能为 null。

widgets/Flex/getEffectiveTextDirection.h.1: 此值由 textDirection 属性和环境中的 Directionality 推导得出。如果无需指定文本方向，则此值为 null。实际上，通常都需要指定方向；例外是垂直 Flex（例如 Column），且其 crossAxisAlignment 不依赖文本方向（不是 start 或 end）。特别是，Row 始终需要文本方向，因为文本方向会控制其布局顺序。（对 Column 而言，布局顺序由 verticalDirection 控制；它总会被指定，因为不依赖继承的 widget，且默认值为 VerticalDirection.down。）
widgets/Flex/getEffectiveTextDirection.h.2: 此方法使 Flex 的子类能够创建基于 RenderFlex 的自定义渲染对象，同时复用仅在必要时提供文本方向的逻辑。

widgets/Flex/mainAxisAlignment.html.1: 例如，默认值 MainAxisAlignment.start 会将子项放在主轴起点（即 Row 中的左侧，或 Column 中的顶部）。

widgets/Flex/mainAxisSize.html.1: 为子项分配空间后，可能仍有剩余空闲空间。此值会在满足传入布局约束的前提下，控制是尽量占满还是尽量缩小这部分空间。
widgets/Flex/mainAxisSize.html.2: 如果某些子项的 flex 因子非零，且没有子项采用 FlexFit.loose，它们会扩展以占用所有可用空间，因此没有剩余空闲空间可供扩大或缩小；此时该值对最终布局没有影响。

widgets/Flex/spacing.html.1: 此间距仅应用于主轴上的子项之间。
widgets/Flex/spacing.html.6: 如果 spacing 为 10.0 且 mainAxisAlignment 为 MainAxisAlignment.spaceAround，主轴上每个子项之间至少会有 10.0 像素间距，其余空闲空间会分配到子项之间，以及第一个子项之前和最后一个子项之后。此处指定的 spacing 本身不会应用在第一个子项之前或最后一个子项之后。
widgets/Flex/spacing.html.7: 如果 spacing 为 10.0 且 mainAxisAlignment 为 MainAxisAlignment.spaceEvenly，主轴上每个子项之间至少会有 10.0 像素间距，其余空闲空间会均匀分配到子项之间，以及第一个子项之前和最后一个子项之后。此处指定的 spacing 本身不会应用在首尾子项之外。
widgets/Flex/spacing.html.8: spacing 非零时，布局尺寸会大于子项沿主轴的布局尺寸之和。
widgets/Flex/spacing.html.9: 如果子项布局尺寸总和与子项间距总和大于主轴上的最大约束，子项就会溢出。例如，有两个子项，最大约束为 100.0 像素，每个子项的布局尺寸为 50.0 像素，间距为 10.0 像素，则子项会溢出 10.0 像素。

widgets/Flex/textBaseline.html.0: 按基线对齐项目时所使用的基线。
widgets/Flex/textBaseline.html.1: 使用基线对齐时必须设置此项。此处没有默认值，因为框架无法预先知道正确的基线。

This example shows best practices for implementing debugFillProperties illustrating use of all common DiagnosticsProperty subclasses and all common DiagnosticsProperty parameters.
link 
class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

This example shows best practices for implementing debugFillProperties illustrating use of all common DiagnosticsProperty subclasses and all common DiagnosticsProperty parameters.
link 
class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

widgets/FocusManager/dispose.html.0: 释放此对象使用的所有资源。

widgets/FocusManager/FocusManager.html.0: 创建一个管理焦点树的对象。

widgets/FocusManager/FocusManager.html.2: 新建的焦点管理器尚未注册用于管理焦点所必需的事件处理器。调用方必须调用 registerGlobalHandlers 注册这些处理器。有关需要注意事项，请参阅该方法的文档。

widgets/FocusManager/highlightMode.html.1: 返回值取决于所使用的 highlightStrategy，也可能取决于用户最近使用的交互模式（具体取决于 highlightStrategy 的值）。
widgets/FocusManager/highlightMode.html.2: 如果 highlightMode 返回 FocusHighlightMode.touch，widget 不应绘制焦点高亮，除非它们需要进行文本输入。
widgets/FocusManager/highlightMode.html.3: 如果 highlightMode 返回 FocusHighlightMode.traditional，widget 在获得焦点时应显示焦点高亮。

widgets/FocusManager/highlightStrategy.h.1: 设为 FocusHighlightStrategy.automatic 时，高亮模式会根据最近使用的交互模式变化。例如，最近一次交互是触摸时，highlightMode 会返回 FocusHighlightMode.touch，只有会弹出软键盘的 widget 才显示焦点高亮。最近一次交互不是触摸（例如按下硬件键盘或点击鼠标）时，highlightMode 会返回 FocusHighlightMode.traditional，所有 widget 都会显示焦点高亮。
widgets/FocusManager/highlightStrategy.h.2: 设为 FocusHighlightStrategy.alwaysTouch 或 FocusHighlightStrategy.alwaysTraditional 时，无论最近一次 UI 交互的类型是什么，highlightMode 始终分别返回 FocusHighlightMode.touch 或 FocusHighlightMode.traditional。

This example shows best practices for implementing debugFillProperties illustrating use of all common DiagnosticsProperty subclasses and all common DiagnosticsProperty parameters.
link 
class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

widgets/FocusNode/descendantsAreFocusabl.4: 更改此值导致后代节点失去焦点时，焦点会移动到包含此节点的范围。

widgets/FocusNode/descendantsAreTraversa.0: 为 false 时，会告知焦点遍历策略在遍历过程中跳过此节点的所有后代。

widgets/FocusNode/descendantsAreTraversa.2: 此项不影响后代的 FocusNode.skipTraversal 值，也不影响后代是否能够获得焦点。

widgets/FocusNode/dispose.html.0: 释放此对象使用的所有资源。

widgets/FocusNode/enclosingScope.html.0: 返回此节点上方最近的外层范围节点；如果节点尚未加入焦点树，则返回 null。
widgets/FocusNode/enclosingScope.html.1: 如果此节点本身是范围节点，此属性只会返回该范围的祖先。
widgets/FocusNode/enclosingScope.html.2: 若要从此节点本身开始查找，请使用 nearestScope。

widgets/FocusNode/focusInDirection.html.0: 通过调用 FocusTraversalPolicy.inDirection，请求将焦点移到给定方向上最近的焦点节点。

widgets/FocusNode/FocusNode.html.2: 若要接收发往此节点的按键事件，请向 onKeyEvent 传入监听器。

widgets/FocusNode/hasFocus.html.1: 当 FocusNode 是某个 hasPrimaryFocus 返回 true 的节点的祖先，或节点本身拥有主要焦点时，它就拥有焦点。
widgets/FocusNode/hasFocus.html.2: hasFocus 与 hasPrimaryFocus 不同：只要节点位于焦点链的任意位置，hasFocus 就为 true；而 hasPrimaryFocus 只有在节点位于焦点链末端时才返回 true。
widgets/FocusNode/hasFocus.html.3: 如果某节点的 hasFocus 返回 true，且其拥有焦点的后代节点都没有通过已弃用的 onKey 处理器处理事件，该节点就会接收按键事件。
widgets/FocusNode/hasFocus.html.4: 此对象是 ChangeNotifier；每当此值变化时，都会通知其 Listenable 监听器（通过 addListener 注册）。

widgets/FocusNode/hasPrimaryFocus.html.0: 如果此节点当前拥有应用范围的输入焦点，则返回 true。
widgets/FocusNode/hasPrimaryFocus.html.1: 当此节点在最近的祖先 FocusScopeNode 中处于焦点状态，且其所有祖先节点的 hasFocus 均为 true，而其后代节点均未处于焦点状态时，此 FocusNode 就拥有主要焦点。
widgets/FocusNode/hasPrimaryFocus.html.2: 这与 hasFocus 不同：只要节点位于焦点链的任意位置，hasFocus 就为 true；而此处要求节点位于焦点链末端才返回 true。
widgets/FocusNode/hasPrimaryFocus.html.3: hasPrimaryFocus 返回 true 的节点，会最先通过其已弃用的 onKey 处理器接收按键事件。
widgets/FocusNode/hasPrimaryFocus.html.4: 每当此值变化时，此对象都会通知其监听器。

widgets/FocusNode/nearestScope.html.0: 返回此节点上方最近的外层范围节点；如果此节点本身是范围节点，也会将其纳入查找范围。

widgets/FocusNode/onKey.html.0: 此焦点节点在拥有焦点时（即 hasFocus 返回 true 时）收到按键事件，就会调用此回调。

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

This example shows best practices for implementing debugFillProperties illustrating use of all common DiagnosticsProperty subclasses and all common DiagnosticsProperty parameters.
link 
class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

This example shows best practices for implementing debugFillProperties illustrating use of all common DiagnosticsProperty subclasses and all common DiagnosticsProperty parameters.
link 
class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

widgets/IconData/hashCode.html.3: If operator == is overridden to use the object state instead, the hash code must also be changed to represent that state, otherwise the object cannot be used in hash based data structures like the default Set 和 Map implementations.
widgets/IconData/hashCode.html.5: 不相等的对象可以具有相同的哈希码。理论上甚至允许所有实例都使用同一哈希码；但如果冲突过于频繁，可能降低 HashSet 或 HashMap 等基于哈希的数据结构的效率。
widgets/IconData/hashCode.html.1: 哈希码是一个整数，用于表示会影响 operator == 比较的对象状态。
widgets/IconData/hashCode.html.2: 所有对象都有哈希码。Object 实现的默认哈希码只表示对象标识；同样，默认的 operator == 仅在两个对象相同（参见 identityHashCode）时才认为它们相等。
widgets/IconData/hashCode.html.4: 相等对象必须具有相同的哈希码（相等性由 operator == 判断）。只有当对象发生影响相等性的变化时，它的哈希码才应改变。除此之外，没有关于哈希码的其他要求；同一程序的不同运行之间无需保持一致，也不保证分布特性。
widgets/IconData/hashCode.html.6: 如果子类重写了 hashCode，也应重写 operator == 运算符，以保持一致性。

widgets/IconData/operator_equals.html.1: 所有 Object 的默认行为都是：仅当此对象与 other 是同一个对象时才返回 true。
widgets/IconData/operator_equals.html.2: 重写此方法可以为类指定不同的相等关系，但该关系仍必须满足等价关系，也就是说必须满足以下条件：
widgets/IconData/operator_equals.html.3: 完备性：对所有参数都必须返回布尔值，且不应抛出异常。
widgets/IconData/operator_equals.html.4: 自反性：对所有对象 o，o == o 都必须为 true。
widgets/IconData/operator_equals.html.5: 对称性：对所有对象 o1 和 o2，o1 == o2 与 o2 == o1 必须同时为 true 或同时为 false。
widgets/IconData/operator_equals.html.6: 传递性：对所有对象 o1、o2 和 o3，若 o1 == o2 且 o2 == o3 为 true，则 o1 == o3 也必须为 true。
widgets/IconData/operator_equals.html.7: 此方法还应随时间保持一致：只有至少一个对象发生更改时，两个对象是否相等才应改变。
widgets/IconData/operator_equals.html.8: 如果子类重写了相等运算符，也应重写 hashCode 方法，以保持一致性。
