class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

rendering/RelayoutWhenSystemFontsChangeM.1: 哈希码是一个整数，表示对象中影响 operator == 比较的状态。
rendering/RelayoutWhenSystemFontsChangeM.2: 所有对象都有哈希码。Object 实现的默认哈希码只表示对象的身份，这与默认的 operator == 实现只在对象相同时才认为它们相等的方式一致（参见 identityHashCode）。
rendering/RelayoutWhenSystemFontsChangeM.3: 如果重写 operator == 以改为使用对象状态，那么哈希码也必须随之更改以表示该状态，否则该对象就无法用于基于哈希的数据结构，例如默认的 Set 和 Map 实现。
rendering/RelayoutWhenSystemFontsChangeM.4: 彼此相等（依据 operator ==）的对象必须具有相同的哈希码。对象的哈希码只应在对象以影响相等性的方式发生变化时才改变。哈希码没有其他要求。它们不需要在程序的多次执行之间保持一致，也没有分布方面的保证。
rendering/RelayoutWhenSystemFontsChangeM.5: 不相等的对象可以具有相同的哈希码。理论上甚至允许所有实例都使用同一哈希码；但如果冲突过于频繁，可能降低 HashSet 或 HashMap 等基于哈希的数据结构的效率。
rendering/RelayoutWhenSystemFontsChangeM.6: 如果子类重写了 hashCode，那么它也应该重写 operator == 运算符以保持一致性。

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

rendering/RendererBinding/hashCode.html.1: 哈希码是一个整数，表示对象中影响 operator == 比较的状态。
rendering/RendererBinding/hashCode.html.2: 所有对象都有哈希码。Object 实现的默认哈希码只表示对象的身份，这与默认的 operator == 实现只在对象相同时才认为它们相等的方式一致（参见 identityHashCode）。
rendering/RendererBinding/hashCode.html.3: 如果重写 operator == 以改为使用对象状态，那么哈希码也必须随之更改以表示该状态，否则该对象就无法用于基于哈希的数据结构，例如默认的 Set 和 Map 实现。
rendering/RendererBinding/hashCode.html.4: 彼此相等（依据 operator ==）的对象必须具有相同的哈希码。对象的哈希码只应在对象以影响相等性的方式发生变化时才改变。哈希码没有其他要求。它们不需要在程序的多次执行之间保持一致，也没有分布方面的保证。
rendering/RendererBinding/hashCode.html.5: 不相等的对象可以具有相同的哈希码。理论上甚至允许所有实例都使用同一哈希码；但如果冲突过于频繁，可能降低 HashSet 或 HashMap 等基于哈希的数据结构的效率。
rendering/RendererBinding/hashCode.html.6: 如果子类重写了 hashCode，那么它也应该重写 operator == 运算符以保持一致性。

rendering/RendererBinding/operator_equal.5: 对称性：对所有对象 o1 和 o2，o1 == o2 与 o2 == o1 必须同时为 true 或同时为 false。
rendering/RendererBinding/operator_equal.6: 传递性：对所有对象 o1、o2 和 o3，若 o1 == o2 且 o2 == o3 为 true，则 o1 == o3 也必须为 true。
rendering/RendererBinding/operator_equal.7: 此方法还应随时间保持一致：只有至少一个对象发生更改时，两个对象是否相等才应改变。
rendering/RendererBinding/operator_equal.8: 如果子类重写了相等运算符，它也应该重写 hashCode 方法，以保持一致性。

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

rendering/RenderInlineChildrenContainerD.1: 哈希码是一个整数，表示对象中影响 operator == 比较的状态。
rendering/RenderInlineChildrenContainerD.2: 所有对象都有哈希码。Object 实现的默认哈希码只表示对象的身份，这与默认的 operator == 实现只在对象相同时才认为它们相等的方式一致（参见 identityHashCode）。
rendering/RenderInlineChildrenContainerD.3: 如果重写 operator == 以改为使用对象状态，那么哈希码也必须随之更改以表示该状态，否则该对象就无法用于基于哈希的数据结构，例如默认的 Set 和 Map 实现。
rendering/RenderInlineChildrenContainerD.4: 彼此相等（依据 operator ==）的对象必须具有相同的哈希码。对象的哈希码只应在对象以影响相等性的方式发生变化时才改变。哈希码没有其他要求。它们不需要在程序的多次执行之间保持一致，也没有分布方面的保证。
rendering/RenderInlineChildrenContainerD.5: 不相等的对象可以具有相同的哈希码。理论上甚至允许所有实例都使用同一哈希码；但如果冲突过于频繁，可能降低 HashSet 或 HashMap 等基于哈希的数据结构的效率。
rendering/RenderInlineChildrenContainerD.6: 如果子类重写了 hashCode，那么它也应该重写 operator == 运算符以保持一致性。

rendering/RenderInlineChildrenContainerD.3: 完备性：对所有参数都必须返回布尔值，且不应抛出异常。
rendering/RenderInlineChildrenContainerD.4: 自反性：对所有对象 o，o == o 都必须为 true。
rendering/RenderInlineChildrenContainerD.5: 对称性：对所有对象 o1 和 o2，o1 == o2 与 o2 == o1 必须同时为 true 或同时为 false。
rendering/RenderInlineChildrenContainerD.6: 传递性：对所有对象 o1、o2 和 o3，若 o1 == o2 且 o2 == o3 为 true，则 o1 == o3 也必须为 true。
rendering/RenderInlineChildrenContainerD.7: 此方法还应随时间保持一致：只有至少一个对象发生更改时，两个对象是否相等才应改变。
rendering/RenderInlineChildrenContainerD.8: 如果子类重写了相等运算符，它也应该重写 hashCode 方法，以保持一致性。

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

rendering/RenderObjectWithChildMixin/has.1: 哈希码是一个整数，表示对象中影响 operator == 比较的状态。
rendering/RenderObjectWithChildMixin/has.2: 所有对象都有哈希码。Object 实现的默认哈希码只表示对象的身份，这与默认的 operator == 实现只在对象相同时才认为它们相等的方式一致（参见 identityHashCode）。
rendering/RenderObjectWithChildMixin/has.3: 如果重写 operator == 以改为使用对象状态，那么哈希码也必须随之更改以表示该状态，否则该对象就无法用于基于哈希的数据结构，例如默认的 Set 和 Map 实现。
rendering/RenderObjectWithChildMixin/has.4: 彼此相等（依据 operator ==）的对象必须具有相同的哈希码。对象的哈希码只应在对象以影响相等性的方式发生变化时才改变。哈希码没有其他要求。它们不需要在程序的多次执行之间保持一致，也没有分布方面的保证。
rendering/RenderObjectWithChildMixin/has.5: 不相等的对象可以具有相同的哈希码。理论上甚至允许所有实例都使用同一哈希码；但如果冲突过于频繁，可能降低 HashSet 或 HashMap 等基于哈希的数据结构的效率。
rendering/RenderObjectWithChildMixin/has.6: 如果子类重写了 hashCode，那么它也应该重写 operator == 运算符以保持一致性。

rendering/RenderObjectWithChildMixin/noS.0: 访问不存在的方法或属性时调用。
rendering/RenderObjectWithChildMixin/noS.1: 动态成员调用可能会尝试调用接收对象上并不存在的成员。示例：
rendering/RenderObjectWithChildMixin/noS.2: 这段无效代码会对整数 1 调用 noSuchMethod 方法，并传入一个表示 .add(42) 调用及其参数的 Invocation（随后会抛出异常）。
rendering/RenderObjectWithChildMixin/noS.3: 类可以重写 noSuchMethod，为这类无效的动态调用提供自定义行为。
rendering/RenderObjectWithChildMixin/noS.4: 如果一个类具有非默认的 noSuchMethod 调用，它也可以省略其接口成员的实现。示例：
rendering/RenderObjectWithChildMixin/noS.5: 尽管 MockList 类没有实现 List 接口的任何方法，这段代码在编译时也没有任何警告或错误。对 List 方法的调用会被转发到 noSuchMethod，因此这段代码会 log 一个类似 Invocation.method(#add, [42]) 的调用，然后抛出异常。

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/hashCode.h.1: 哈希码是一个整数，表示对象中影响 operator == 比较的状态。
rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/hashCode.h.2: 所有对象都有哈希码。Object 实现的默认哈希码只表示对象的身份，这与默认的 operator == 实现只在对象相同时才认为它们相等的方式一致（参见 identityHashCode）。
rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/hashCode.h.3: 如果重写 operator == 以改为使用对象状态，那么哈希码也必须随之更改以表示该状态，否则该对象就无法用于基于哈希的数据结构，例如默认的 Set 和 Map 实现。
rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/hashCode.h.4: 彼此相等（依据 operator ==）的对象必须具有相同的哈希码。对象的哈希码只应在对象以影响相等性的方式发生变化时才改变。哈希码没有其他要求。它们不需要在程序的多次执行之间保持一致，也没有分布方面的保证。
rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/hashCode.h.5: 不相等的对象可以具有相同的哈希码。理论上甚至允许所有实例都使用同一哈希码；但如果冲突过于频繁，可能降低 HashSet 或 HashMap 等基于哈希的数据结构的效率。
rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/hashCode.h.6: 如果子类重写了 hashCode，那么它也应该重写 operator == 运算符以保持一致性。

rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/operator_e.1: 所有 Object 的默认行为都是：仅当此对象与 other 是同一个对象时才返回 true。
rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/operator_e.2: 重写此方法可以为类指定不同的相等关系，但该关系仍必须满足等价关系，也就是说必须满足以下条件：
rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/operator_e.3: 完备性：对所有参数都必须返回布尔值，且不应抛出异常。
rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/operator_e.4: 自反性：对所有对象 o，o == o 都必须为 true。
rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/operator_e.5: 对称性：对所有对象 o1 和 o2，o1 == o2 与 o2 == o1 必须同时为 true 或同时为 false。
rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/operator_e.6: 传递性：对所有对象 o1、o2 和 o3，若 o1 == o2 且 o2 == o3 为 true，则 o1 == o3 也必须为 true。
rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/operator_e.7: 此方法还应随时间保持一致：只有至少一个对象发生更改时，两个对象是否相等才应改变。
rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/operator_e.8: 如果子类重写了相等运算符，它也应该重写 hashCode 方法，以保持一致性。

rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/toString.h.1: 有些类具有默认的文本表示，通常还提供一个静态 parse 函数（例如 int.parse）。这些类会使用该文本表示作为其字符串表示。
rendering/RenderProxyBoxMixin/toString.h.2: 其他类没有程序需要关注的、有实际意义的文本表示。这些类通常会重写 toString，以便在检查对象时提供有用的信息，主要用于调试或日志记录。

The following is an example of how to go from a GlobalKey on a RepaintBoundary to a PNG:
link 
class PngHome extends StatefulWidget {
  const PngHome({super.key});

  @override
  State<PngHome> createState() => _PngHomeState();
}

class _PngHomeState extends State<PngHome> {
  GlobalKey globalKey = GlobalKey();

  Future<void> _capturePng() async {
    final RenderRepaintBoundary boundary = globalKey.currentContext!.findRenderObject()! as RenderRepaintBoundary;
    final ui.Image image = await boundary.toImage();
    final ByteData? byteData = await image.toByteData(format: ui.ImageByteFormat.png);
    final Uint8List pngBytes = byteData!.buffer.asUint8List();
    print(pngBytes);
  }

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return RepaintBoundary(
      key: globalKey,
      child: Center(
        child: TextButton(
          onPressed: _capturePng,
          child: const Text('Hello World', textDirection: TextDirection.ltr),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

This example shows best practices for implementing debugFillProperties illustrating use of all common DiagnosticsProperty subclasses and all common DiagnosticsProperty parameters.

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

rendering/TransformLayer/debugFillProper.6: 如果这些子类都不适用，可以直接使用 DiagnosticsProperty 构造函数；少数情况下，也可以像 TransformProperty 那样创建自己的 DiagnosticsProperty 子类，以处理表示变换的 Matrix4。通常，只要属性值实现了良好的 toString 方法，直接使用 DiagnosticsProperty 就可以正常工作。
rendering/TransformLayer/debugFillProper.7:
This example shows best practices for implementing debugFillProperties illustrating use of all common DiagnosticsProperty subclasses and all common DiagnosticsProperty parameters.
link 
class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

painting/AlignmentGeometry/hashCode.html.1: 哈希码是一个整数，用于表示会影响 operator == 比较结果的对象状态。
painting/AlignmentGeometry/hashCode.html.2: 所有对象都有哈希码。Object 默认实现的哈希码仅表示对象标识；同样，operator == 的默认实现也只会在两个对象是同一对象时才认为它们相等（参见 identityHashCode）。
painting/AlignmentGeometry/hashCode.html.3: 如果重写 operator ==，使其根据对象状态进行比较，也必须修改哈希码以表示该状态；否则，该对象无法用于基于哈希的集合，例如默认的 Set 和 Map 实现。
painting/AlignmentGeometry/hashCode.html.4: 根据 operator == 判定为相等的对象必须具有相同的哈希码。只有当对象发生影响相等性判断的变化时，其哈希码才应改变。除此之外，哈希码没有其他要求：同一程序的不同运行之间不必保持一致，也不保证特定的分布情况。
painting/AlignmentGeometry/hashCode.html.5: 不相等的对象可以具有相同的哈希码。理论上甚至允许所有实例都使用同一哈希码；但如果冲突过于频繁，可能降低 HashSet 或 HashMap 等基于哈希的数据结构的效率。
painting/AlignmentGeometry/hashCode.html.6: 如果子类重写了 hashCode，也应重写 operator ==，以保持一致性。

painting/AlignmentGeometry/operator_equa.1: 所有 Object 的默认行为都是：仅当此对象与 other 是同一个对象时才返回 true。
painting/AlignmentGeometry/operator_equa.2: 重写此方法可以为类指定不同的相等关系，但该关系仍必须满足等价关系，也就是说必须满足以下条件：
painting/AlignmentGeometry/operator_equa.3: 完备性：对所有参数都必须返回布尔值，且不应抛出异常。
painting/AlignmentGeometry/operator_equa.4: 自反性：对所有对象 o，o == o 都必须为 true。
painting/AlignmentGeometry/operator_equa.5: 对称性：对所有对象 o1 和 o2，o1 == o2 与 o2 == o1 必须同时为 true 或同时为 false。

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

This example shows best practices for implementing debugFillProperties illustrating use of all common DiagnosticsProperty subclasses and all common DiagnosticsProperty parameters.
link 
class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

painting/ColorSwatch/hashCode.html.6: 如果子类重写了 hashCode，也应重写 operator ==，以保持一致性。
