PageRouteBuilder<void>(
  pageBuilder: (BuildContext context,
      Animation<double> animation,
      Animation<double> secondaryAnimation,
  ) {
    return Scaffold(
      appBar: AppBar(title: const Text('Hello')),
      body: const Center(
        child: Text('Hello World'),
      ),
    );
  },
  transitionsBuilder: (
      BuildContext context,
      Animation<double> animation,
      Animation<double> secondaryAnimation,
      Widget child,
  ) {
    return SlideTransition(
      position: Tween<Offset>(
        begin: const Offset(0.0, 1.0),
        end: Offset.zero,
      ).animate(animation),
      child: SlideTransition(
        position: Tween<Offset>(
          begin: Offset.zero,
          end: const Offset(0.0, 1.0),
        ).animate(secondaryAnimation),
        child: child,
      ),
     );
  },
)

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

class MyWidget extends StatefulWidget {
  const MyWidget({super.key, this.onPressed});

  /// Something important this widget must do when pressed.
  final VoidCallback? onPressed;

  @override
  State<MyWidget> createState() => MyWidgetState();
}

class MyWidgetState extends State<MyWidget> with MaterialStateMixin<MyWidget> {
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return ColoredBox(
      color: isPressed ? Colors.black : Colors.white,
      child: InkWell(
        onHighlightChanged: updateMaterialState(
          WidgetState.pressed,
          onChanged: (bool val) {
            if (val) {
              widget.onPressed?.call();
            }
          },
        ),
      ),
    );

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

MenuAnchor(

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.

    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view

      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null

        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

material/OutlineInputBorder/hashCode.htm.1: 哈希码是一个整数，用于表示会影响 operator == 比较结果的对象状态。
material/OutlineInputBorder/hashCode.htm.2: 所有对象都有哈希码。Object 的默认哈希码仅表示对象的标识；同样，默认的 operator == 实现也只有在两个对象完全相同时才认为它们相等（参见 identityHashCode）。

material/OutlineInputBorder/hashCode.htm.4: 根据 operator == 判定为相等的对象，其哈希码必须相同。只有当对象发生影响相等性判断的变化时，其哈希码才应改变。除此之外，哈希码没有其他要求：不同程序运行之间不必保持一致，也不保证哈希值的分布特性。
material/OutlineInputBorder/hashCode.htm.5: 不相等的对象可以具有相同的哈希码。理论上甚至允许所有实例都使用同一哈希码；但如果冲突过于频繁，可能降低 HashSet 或 HashMap 等基于哈希的数据结构的效率。

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

material/PageTransitionsTheme/hashCode.h.4: 根据 operator == 判定为相等的对象，其哈希码必须相同。只有当对象发生影响相等性判断的变化时，其哈希码才应改变。除此之外，哈希码没有其他要求：不同程序运行之间不必保持一致，也不保证哈希值的分布特性。
material/PageTransitionsTheme/hashCode.h.5: 不相等的对象可以具有相同的哈希码。理论上甚至允许所有实例都使用同一哈希码；但如果冲突过于频繁，可能降低 HashSet 或 HashMap 等基于哈希的数据结构的效率。

material/PageTransitionsTheme/operator_e.1: 所有 Object 的默认行为都是：仅当此对象与 other 是同一个对象时才返回 true。

material/PaginatedDataTableState/build.h.0: 描述此 widget 所表示的用户界面部分。
material/PaginatedDataTableState/build.h.1: 框架会在多种不同情况下调用此方法，例如：
material/PaginatedDataTableState/build.h.2: 此方法可能在每一帧中调用，因此除构建组件外，不应产生任何副作用。
material/PaginatedDataTableState/build.h.3: 框架会将此 widget 下方的子树替换为此方法返回的 widget。根据返回的 widget 是否能够更新现有子树的根节点（由调用 Widget.canUpdate 判定），框架会更新现有子树，或移除它并重新创建子树。

material/PaginatedDataTableState/build.h.5: 给定的 BuildContext 包含此组件在组件树中构建位置的信息。例如，context 会提供该位置上的继承组件集合。此 BuildContext 参数始终与此 State 对象的 context 属性相同，并在该对象的整个生命周期内保持不变。此处冗余地提供 BuildContext 参数，是为了使此方法与 WidgetBuilder 的签名一致。
material/PaginatedDataTableState/build.h.7: 为什么 build 方法位于 State 上，而不是 StatefulWidget 上？
material/PaginatedDataTableState/build.h.8: 将 Widget build(BuildContext context) 方法放在 State 上，而不是在 StatefulWidget 上放置 Widget build(BuildContext context, State state) 方法，可以让开发者在继承 StatefulWidget 时拥有更大的灵活性。
material/PaginatedDataTableState/build.h.9: 例如，AnimatedWidget 是 StatefulWidget 的子类，它声明了一个抽象的 Widget build(BuildContext context) 方法供子类实现。如果 StatefulWidget 已经有一个接收 State 参数的 build 方法，那么 AnimatedWidget 就不得不将其 State 对象提供给子类，即使该 State 对象只是 AnimatedWidget 的内部实现细节。
material/PaginatedDataTableState/build.h.10: 从概念上说，StatelessWidget 也可以用类似方式实现为 StatefulWidget 的子类。如果 build 方法位于 State 上，而不是 StatefulWidget 上，这种实现就不再可行。
material/PaginatedDataTableState/build.h.11: 将 build 函数放在 State 而不是 StatefulWidget 上，还有助于避免一类与闭包隐式捕获 this 有关的错误。如果在 StatefulWidget 上定义的 build 函数中创建闭包，该闭包会隐式捕获 this，也就是当前组件实例，并能访问该实例不可变的字段：
material/PaginatedDataTableState/build.h.12: 例如，假设父组件以蓝色的 color 构建 MyButton，那么打印函数中的 $color 会如预期一样表示蓝色。之后，假设父组件以绿色重新构建 MyButton。第一次构建时创建的闭包仍会隐式引用原组件，因此即使组件已更新为绿色，$color 仍会打印蓝色；如果该闭包的生命周期超过组件本身，它就会打印过时的信息。
material/PaginatedDataTableState/build.h.13: 相反，如果 build 函数位于 State 对象上，那么在 build 期间创建的闭包会隐式捕获 State 实例，而不是组件实例：
material/PaginatedDataTableState/build.h.14: 现在，父组件以绿色重新构建 MyButton 时，第一次构建创建的闭包仍引用在重建期间保持不变的 State 对象；但框架已将该 State 对象的 widget 属性更新为新的 MyButton 实例，因此 ${widget.color} 会如预期一样打印绿色。

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

material/PopupMenuThemeData/hashCode.htm.5: 不相等的对象可以具有相同的哈希码。理论上甚至允许所有实例都使用同一哈希码；但如果冲突过于频繁，可能降低 HashSet 或 HashMap 等基于哈希的数据结构的效率。
material/PopupMenuThemeData/hashCode.htm.6: 如果子类重写了 hashCode，也应重写 operator == 运算符，以保持一致。

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

此示例展示了实现 debugFillProperties 的最佳实践， 演示了所有常见 DiagnosticsProperty 子类以及所有常见 DiagnosticsProperty 参数的用法。
link 
class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

material/RangeSlider/debugFillProperties.7:
此示例展示了实现 debugFillProperties 的最佳实践， 演示了所有常见 DiagnosticsProperty 子类以及所有常见 DiagnosticsProperty 参数的用法。
link 
class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

material/RangeValues/hashCode.html.1: 哈希码是一个整数，用于表示会影响 operator == 比较结果的对象状态。
material/RangeValues/hashCode.html.2: 所有对象都有哈希码。Object 默认实现的哈希码只表示对象标识；同样，operator == 的默认实现也只在对象完全相同（参见 identityHashCode）时才认为它们相等。
material/RangeValues/hashCode.html.3: 如果重写 operator ==，使其依据对象状态进行比较，也必须修改哈希码以表示该状态，否则此对象将无法用于基于哈希的集合，例如默认的 Set 和 Map 实现。
material/RangeValues/hashCode.html.4: 根据 operator == 判定为相等的对象必须具有相同的哈希码。只有当对象发生影响相等性判断的变化时，其哈希码才应改变。除此之外，哈希码没有其他要求。不同次运行同一程序时，哈希码不必保持一致，也不保证其分布特性。
material/RangeValues/hashCode.html.5: 不相等的对象可以具有相同的哈希码。理论上甚至允许所有实例都使用同一哈希码；但如果冲突过于频繁，可能降低 HashSet 或 HashMap 等基于哈希的数据结构的效率。
material/RangeValues/hashCode.html.6: 如果子类重写了 hashCode，也应重写 operator == 运算符，以保持一致。

material/RangeValues/operator_equals.htm.1: 所有 Object 的默认行为都是：仅当此对象与 other 是同一个对象时才返回 true。
material/RangeValues/operator_equals.htm.2: 重写此方法可以为类指定不同的相等关系，但该关系仍必须满足等价关系，也就是说必须满足以下条件：
material/RangeValues/operator_equals.htm.3: 完备性：对所有参数都必须返回布尔值，且不应抛出异常。
material/RangeValues/operator_equals.htm.4: 自反性：对所有对象 o，o == o 都必须为 true。
material/RangeValues/operator_equals.htm.5: 对称性：对所有对象 o1 和 o2，o1 == o2 与 o2 == o1 必须同时为 true 或同时为 false。
material/RangeValues/operator_equals.htm.6: 传递性：对所有对象 o1、o2 和 o3，若 o1 == o2 且 o2 == o3 为 true，则 o1 == o3 也必须为 true。
material/RangeValues/operator_equals.htm.7: 此方法还应随时间保持一致：只有至少一个对象发生更改时，两个对象是否相等才应改变。
material/RangeValues/operator_equals.htm.8: 如果子类重写了相等运算符，也应重写 hashCode 方法，以保持一致。

class Wood extends StatefulWidget {
  const Wood({super.key});

  @override
  State<StatefulWidget> createState() => WoodState();
}

class WoodState extends State<Wood> {
  bool _useChisel = false;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return InputChip(
      label: const Text('Use Chisel'),
      selected: _useChisel,
      onSelected: (bool newValue) {
        setState(() {
          _useChisel = newValue;
        });
      },
    );
  }
}

material/RefreshIndicatorState/build.htm.8: 将 Widget build(BuildContext context) 方法定义在 State 上，而不是将 Widget build(BuildContext context, State state) 方法定义在 StatefulWidget 上，可以让开发者在继承 StatefulWidget 时拥有更大的灵活性。

material/RefreshIndicatorState/build.htm.12: 例如，假设父组件构建 MyButton 时将 color 设为蓝色，那么打印函数中的 $color 会如预期一样指向蓝色。现在假设父组件重建 MyButton 并将其颜色设为绿色。第一次构建创建的闭包仍隐式引用原来的 Widget，因此即使 Widget 已更新为绿色，$color 打印的仍是蓝色；如果该闭包的生命周期超过了 Widget，它就会打印过时的信息。
material/RefreshIndicatorState/build.htm.13: 相反，如果将 build 函数放在 State 对象上，build 期间创建的闭包会隐式捕获 State 实例，而不是 Widget 实例：
material/RefreshIndicatorState/build.htm.14: 现在父组件将 MyButton 重建为绿色时，第一次构建创建的闭包仍引用同一个 State 对象。该对象会在重建期间保留，但框架已更新其 State 对象的 widget 属性，使其指向新的 MyButton 实例，因此 ${widget.color} 会如预期一样打印绿色。

// (e.g. in a stateful widget)

final ScrollController controllerOne = ScrollController();
final ScrollController controllerTwo = ScrollController();

@override
Widget build(BuildContext context) {
  return Column(
    children: <Widget>[
      SizedBox(
       height: 200,
       child: CupertinoScrollbar(
         controller: controllerOne,
         child: ListView.builder(
           controller: controllerOne,
           itemCount: 120,
           itemBuilder: (BuildContext context, int index) => Text('item $index'),
         ),
       ),
     ),
     SizedBox(
       height: 200,
       child: CupertinoScrollbar(
         controller: controllerTwo,
         child: ListView.builder(
           controller: controllerTwo,
           itemCount: 120,
           itemBuilder: (BuildContext context, int index) => Text('list 2 item $index'),
         ),
       ),
     ),
   ],
  );
}

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

material/ScrollbarThemeData/hashCode.htm.1: 哈希码是一个整数，用于表示会影响 operator == 比较结果的对象状态。
material/ScrollbarThemeData/hashCode.htm.2: 所有对象都有哈希码。Object 实现的默认哈希码只表示对象的标识；同样，默认的 operator == 实现也只会在两个对象完全相同时才认为它们相等（参见 identityHashCode）。
material/ScrollbarThemeData/hashCode.htm.3: 如果重写 operator ==，使其根据对象状态进行比较，也必须修改哈希码以表示该状态。否则，对象将无法用于基于哈希的结构，例如默认的 Set 和 Map 实现。
material/ScrollbarThemeData/hashCode.htm.4: 根据 operator == 判断为相等的对象必须具有相同的哈希码。只有当对象发生影响相等性判断的变化时，其哈希码才应改变。除此之外，哈希码没有其他要求：同一程序的不同运行之间不必保持一致，也不保证哈希值的分布情况。
material/ScrollbarThemeData/hashCode.htm.5: 不相等的对象可以具有相同的哈希码。理论上甚至允许所有实例都使用同一哈希码；但如果冲突过于频繁，可能降低 HashSet 或 HashMap 等基于哈希的数据结构的效率。
material/ScrollbarThemeData/hashCode.htm.6: 如果子类重写了 hashCode，也应重写 operator == 运算符，以保持一致。

class ExampleObject extends ExampleSuperclass {

  // ...various members and properties...

  @override
  void debugFillProperties(DiagnosticPropertiesBuilder properties) {
    // Always add properties from the base class first.
    super.debugFillProperties(properties);

    // Omit the property name 'message' when displaying this String property
    // as it would just add visual noise.
    properties.add(StringProperty('message', message, showName: false));

    properties.add(DoubleProperty('stepWidth', stepWidth));

    // A scale of 1.0 does nothing so should be hidden.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('scale', scale, defaultValue: 1.0));

    // If the hitTestExtent matches the paintExtent, it is just set to its
    // default value so is not relevant.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('hitTestExtent', hitTestExtent, defaultValue: paintExtent));

    // maxWidth of double.infinity indicates the width is unconstrained and
    // so maxWidth has no impact.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty('maxWidth', maxWidth, defaultValue: double.infinity));

    // Progress is a value between 0 and 1 or null. Showing it as a
    // percentage makes the meaning clear enough that the name can be
    // hidden.
    properties.add(PercentProperty(
      'progress',
      progress,
      showName: false,
      ifNull: '<indeterminate>',
    ));

    // Most text fields have maxLines set to 1.
    properties.add(IntProperty('maxLines', maxLines, defaultValue: 1));

    // Specify the unit as otherwise it would be unclear that time is in
    // milliseconds.
    properties.add(IntProperty('duration', duration.inMilliseconds, unit: 'ms'));

    // Tooltip is used instead of unit for this case as a unit should be a
    // terse description appropriate to display directly after a number
    // without a space.
    properties.add(DoubleProperty(
      'device pixel ratio',
      devicePixelRatio,
      tooltip: 'physical pixels per logical pixel',
    ));

    // Displaying the depth value would be distracting. Instead only display
    // if the depth value is missing.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<int>('depth', depth, ifNull: 'no depth'));

    // bool flag that is only shown when the value is true.
    properties.add(FlagProperty('using primary controller', value: primary));

    properties.add(FlagProperty(
      'isCurrent',
      value: isCurrent,
      ifTrue: 'active',
      ifFalse: 'inactive',
    ));

    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('keepAlive', keepAlive));

    // FlagProperty could have also been used in this case.
    // This option results in the text "obscureText: true" instead
    // of "obscureText" which is a bit more verbose but a bit clearer.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<bool>('obscureText', obscureText, defaultValue: false));

    properties.add(EnumProperty<TextAlign>('textAlign', textAlign, defaultValue: null));
    properties.add(EnumProperty<ImageRepeat>('repeat', repeat, defaultValue: ImageRepeat.noRepeat));

    // Warn users when the widget is missing but do not show the value.
    properties.add(ObjectFlagProperty<Widget>('widget', widget, ifNull: 'no widget'));

    properties.add(IterableProperty<BoxShadow>(
      'boxShadow',
      boxShadow,
      defaultValue: null,
      style: style,
    ));

    // Getting the value of size throws an exception unless hasSize is true.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Size>.lazy(
      'size',
      () => size,
      description: '${ hasSize ? size : "MISSING" }',
    ));

    // If the `toString` method for the property value does not provide a
    // good terse description, write a DiagnosticsProperty subclass as in
    // the case of TransformProperty which displays a nice debugging view
    // of a Matrix4 that represents a transform.
    properties.add(TransformProperty('transform', transform));

    // If the value class has a good `toString` method, use
    // DiagnosticsProperty<YourValueType>. Specifying the value type ensures
    // that debugging tools always know the type of the field and so can
    // provide the right UI affordances. For example, in this case even
    // if color is null, a debugging tool still knows the value is a Color
    // and can display relevant color related UI.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Color>('color', color));

    // Use a custom description to generate a more terse summary than the
    // `toString` method on the map class.
    properties.add(DiagnosticsProperty<Map<Listenable, VoidCallback>>(
      'handles',
      handles,
      description: handles != null
        ? '${handles!.length} active client${ handles!.length == 1 ? "" : "s" }'
        : null,
      ifNull: 'no notifications ever received',
      showName: false,
    ));
  }
}

material/SearchBarThemeData/hashCode.htm.1: 哈希码是一个整数，用于表示会影响 operator == 比较结果的对象状态。
material/SearchBarThemeData/hashCode.htm.2: 所有对象都有哈希码。Object 的默认哈希码只表示对象的标识；同样，默认的 operator == 实现也只会在两个对象完全相同时才认为它们相等（参见 identityHashCode）。
material/SearchBarThemeData/hashCode.htm.3: 如果重写 operator ==，使其根据对象状态进行比较，也必须修改哈希码以表示该状态；否则，该对象将无法用于基于哈希的集合，例如默认的 Set 和 Map 实现。
material/SearchBarThemeData/hashCode.htm.4: 根据 operator == 判断为相等的对象，其哈希码必须相同。只有当对象发生影响相等性判断的变化时，其哈希码才应改变。除此之外，哈希码没有其他要求：不同程序运行之间无需保持一致，也不保证分布特性。
material/SearchBarThemeData/hashCode.htm.5: 不相等的对象可以具有相同的哈希码。理论上甚至允许所有实例都使用同一哈希码；但如果冲突过于频繁，可能降低 HashSet 或 HashMap 等基于哈希的数据结构的效率。
material/SearchBarThemeData/hashCode.htm.6: 如果子类重写了 hashCode，也应重写 operator ==，以保持一致。

material/SearchBarThemeData/lerp.html.0: 在两个 SearchBarThemeData 之间进行线性插值。
material/SearchBarThemeData/lerp.html.1: t 参数表示时间线上的位置：0.0 表示插值尚未开始，返回 a（或与 a 等价的值）；1.0 表示插值完成，返回 b（或与 b 等价的值）；中间值表示处于 a 与 b 之间时间线的相应位置。插值可以外推到 0.0 和 1.0 之外，因此负值及大于 1.0 的值都有效（Curves.elasticInOut 等曲线很容易产生这些值）。
